title: DejaVuzz: Disclosing Transient Execution Bugs with Dynamic Swappable Memory and Differential Information Flow Tracking Assisted Processor Fuzzing
problem: Existing hardware fuzzers for detecting transient execution vulnerabilities (e.g., Spectre, Meltdown variants) suffer from poor microarchitectural controllability and observability: they cannot reliably set up the precise microarchitectural state needed to trigger transient execution paths, nor detect covert information leakage resulting from such paths.
motivation: Transient execution attacks remain a critical threat to modern CPUs, and manual or undirected fuzzing approaches miss subtle variants due to inability to observe information flow at the microarchitectural level.
method: DejaVuzz introduces two synergistic mechanisms: Dynamic Swappable Memory (DSM), which swaps physical memory pages at runtime to precisely control the microarchitectural state of TLBs, caches, and branch predictors needed to trigger transient execution; and Differential Information Flow Tracking (DIFT), which instruments the processor simulator to observe whether secret data leaks through transient microarchitectural side channels. The fuzzer generates test programs that exercise transient execution windows by leveraging DSM to reset microarchitectural state between tests, and uses DIFT differential analysis to detect when information from a secret source reaches an observable side channel (e.g., cache timing). This enables both high coverage and precise detection of leakage.
key_novelty: Combining dynamic swappable memory for microarchitectural state control with differential information flow tracking to achieve both precise transient execution triggering and covert leakage detection in a hardware fuzzer.
contributions: Dynamic Swappable Memory (DSM) mechanism enabling fine-grained microarchitectural state control for transient execution fuzzing
Differential Information Flow Tracking (DIFT) for detecting covert information leakage through transient execution side channels
End-to-end fuzzing framework that discovers transient execution bugs in large-scale out-of-order processor designs
Empirical demonstration of new transient execution vulnerabilities disclosed by the tool

metrics.other: discovered new transient execution bugs; improved bug detection rate and coverage over prior hardware fuzzers (exact numbers not available from abstract)

baselines: prior hardware fuzzing approaches for transient execution
limitations: Not discussed in the abstract; applicability to real silicon (vs. simulation) not stated.
primary_theme: Microarchitecture-aware fuzzing for transient execution vulnerabilities
